To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) we have found that two HDACi, SAHA and romidepsin, but not VAP, indeed inhibit HR and that RAD51 represents a key protein whose inhibition is required in HDACi-mediated synthetic lethality with olaparib in TNBC; 2) overexpression of RAD51 promotes aberrant repair, leading to enhanced polyploidity and a mechanism for resistance to this combination treatment.

(i) HDACi induce a BRCAness-like phenotype in BRCA1-proficient cells, (ii) the combination of HDAC inhibition and PARP inhibition induces a synthetic lethality response in BRCA1-deficient cells, (iii) RAD51 overexpression is a mechanism of resistance for this combination therapy, and (iv) BRCA1-proficiency stabilizes the genome and prevents polyploid formation after combination treatment with the HDACi and the PARPi.
the combination of HDACis and PARPis is effective in TNBC, and the efficacy of the combination therapy is dictated by the expression of key DNA damage repair genes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel therapeutic approaches for the treatment of breast cancer.
the development of novel therapies for triple-negative breast cancer and the discovery of biomarkers that predict response to therapy.
the development of novel therapeutic approaches for the treatment of triple-negative breast cancer, a subtype of breast cancer with the worst prognosis and no targeted therapies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
HDACi and/or PARP inhibitors should not be used as monotherapies in breast cancer.
the combination of HDAC and PARP inhibitors is a promising therapeutic strategy for the treatment of TNBC.
the use of HDACi in combination with PARPi is a promising therapeutic strategy for TNBC, which should be tested in clinical trials.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we found that two of three HDACis tested indeed inhibit HR repair in TNBC cells.
the HDACi-induced synthetic lethality is mediated by a complex interplay between the expression of key HR proteins, which are differentially regulated depending on which HDACi is utilized.

the combination of histone deacetylases inhibitors (HDACis) and PARP inhibitors (PARPi) is an attractive strategy for treating triple-negative breast cancers (TNBC) and that the HDACis romidepsin and suberoylanide hydroxamic are the most promising for combination with the PARPi olaparib.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the combination of histone deacetylases and PARP inhibition is effective in triple-negative breast cancer cells, but only in those cells that are deficient in BRCA1 or BRCA2.
the HDACis SAHA and ROMD, but not VAP, inhibit HR repair and are capable of sensitizing breast cancer cells to PARPi.
the HDACi-induced BRCAness phenotype is a key determinant of synthetic lethality with the PARP inhibitor in TNBC, which can be used to identify the most appropriate patients for this treatment.
